name: Liath Sidhe
body:
LIATH SIDHE
CR 2

You have just the time to notice a strange movement in the tall grass before a little creature springs towards you at full speed, waving a sword almost as tall as itself and crying something like “Hey you! Do you want a face full of head?”

XP 600
CN Diminutive fey
Init +4; Senses low-light vision, portal sense; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 18, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dexterity, +4 size)
hp 19 (2d6+12)
Fort +5, Ref +8, Will +3; +2 racial bonus vs. enchantment and illusion spells and effects
Immune fear

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee claymore +6 (1d6) or unarmed strike +6 (1d3)
Special Attacks headbutt
Space 1 ft.; Reach 0

STATISTICS

Str 11, Dex 18, Con 18, Int 10, Wis 8, Cha 11
Base Atk +2; Cmb +2; Cmd 16
Feats Improved Unarmed Strike, Toughness
Skills Acrobatics +11, Escape Artist +11, Intimidate +6, Knowledge (local) +5, Perception +4, Sleight of Hand +11, Stealth +23, Survival +5; Racial Modifiers +2 Intimidate, +2 Survival
Languages Common, Sylvan (liath sidhe mostly speak their own variant of Sylvan, that is hardly intelligible by not-accustomed humans)
SQ bold thief, uncanny fierceness

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bold Thief (Ex)

Liath sidhe are able to steal even things that are much larger than them. The carrying capacity of a liath sidhe is calculated as if its Strength bonus were 4 higher.

Headbutt (Ex)

Liath sidhe are famous for their hard heads.

A liath sidhe can forfeit its normal attacks in a round to deliver a mighty headbutt. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 points of damage and has the same effects of a monk’s stunning fist ability.

Portal Sense (Su)

Liath sidhe can sense the presence of dimensional portals, gates, or rifts in a 30-ft. radius.

Uncanny Fierceness (Ex)

Liath sidhe are surprisingly strong and resistant for their size. Their Strength and Constitution scores are not limited by size, and the damage they deal with unarmed strikes and natural attacks is calculated as if they were Medium creatures. They also don’t suffer any penalties on their Intimidate skill checks for being smaller than their target.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, band (2-8) or clan (1d100 + 1 skald)
Treasure normal

Liath sidhe, or “blue fairies,” are roguish, warmongering relatives of the more common pixies and atomies who love nothing more than a good brawl, stealing stuff, strong ales, and swearing. A long time ago, they were driven away from the faerie realm (or escaped, as they prefer to say) because they were too unruly and refused to serve any lord or lady.

Since then, they wreak havoc on the mortal world.

Liath sidhe are 6 inches tall on average, with an unkempt bush of red hair on their head and big noses. Their skin appears to be blue at a distance, but that’s just because of the manifold war tattoos on their whole body. A male liath sidhe usually only wears a tattered kilt, ruined in many fighters.

They steal almost everything they need from human villages, mostly food or alcohol, and fight happily and recklessly both with other creatures and among themselves, but are never evil or cruel, though their recklessness can often do even more damage than if they were.

Habitat & Society: A typical liath sidhe clan is composed of an elder ruling couple and their children, plus some elders from the matron’s birth clan who serve as teachers and keepers of history. Most clan members are barbarians/rogues or brawlers/rogues. Female liath sidhe are rare (around 1 every 100 males), and therefore very prized and honoured for their level heads and sensible minds. They leave their clan at a young age to marry into another family and become the matrons of a new generation. A female liath sidhe usually chooses the way of the witch, and is always the chief of the clan she married into; her husband becomes her second in command and first counsellor.

Even rarer are liath sidhe wizards, almost always males.

A clan will often also have a skald; liath sidhe skalds are famous for their dissonant and very loud war hymns that other liath sidhe find very inspiring, and every other race horrific and maddening.

Unusual Familiar: Liath sidhe have a great respect for magic users, and for witches in particular. They can agree to work with a spellcaster for the greater good of their tribe and their home, regardless of their fickle nature. A spellcaster of at least 7th level with the Improved Familiar feat can select a liath sidhe as a familiar, whatever her alignment is.
